# A/B test: LightGBM ranker against RRF

<!-- Generated by `make ab-report` (analysis/ab_report.py). Do not edit by hand. -->

Simulated traffic (`sim/`, design §2.2) on the api with bundle `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d`, the rank-layer experiment split 50 / 50 over all users, the standing campaigns (16) filling the sponsored slots, 16 sessions at a time with pauses of 50-300 ms between page views. The simulator's users click by examination × relevance to their test-period items; it validates the system and the experiment pipeline, while the evidence for the model is the offline evaluation (§2.2). The A/A ran first, and the analysis was checked on it before the A/B was read.

## Setup

| Phase | Experiment | Arms | Traffic | Sessions | Page views | State Redis: evicted / refused | Cache Redis: evicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AA | `rank-aa-v1` | a 50% (rrf), b 50% (rrf) | 20 min | 31,853 | 104,111 | 0 / 0 | 0 |
| AB | `rank-ab-v1` | rrf 50% (rrf), lightgbm 50% (lightgbm) | 20 min | 31,919 | 103,944 | 0 / 0 | 0 |

Each phase started from the same state: the consumers caught up, the cache Redis flushed and the state Redis reseeded with the dataset users' training histories. Unit: the user. Ratio metrics (CTR, add-to-cart rate) are sums per user, the variance of the ratio from the delta method, with a user-level bootstrap interval next to it (B = 2,000); two-sided z-test. Impressions come from the sample job (`ml/samples/job.py`): every impression joined to its served record, labelled by a click within 30 minutes.

## Reading

- Home-feed CTR with the LightGBM ranker is not significantly different from CTR with RRF: +0.0001 (+1.0%), 95% CI [-0.0005, +0.0006], p = 0.743. The interval's half-width, 0.0006 (6% of RRF's CTR), is the size of difference this test could tell from zero.
- Offline (`docs/results/offline.md`, test split): NDCG@10 +0.0186 [+0.0144, +0.0233], HR@10 +0.0199 [+0.0135, +0.0264].
- The offline gain is all in the segment whose target was reviewed on the same day as the last history item (NDCG@10 +0.0381 [+0.0302, +0.0462]; later targets -0.0021 [-0.0053, +0.0014]). The simulator's users click by text relevance to all their test-period items; it does not model what ties a same-day target to the last history item, so a result near zero here matches the later-day segment and says nothing for or against the same-day gain.
- Both arms make the same calls (Rank runs for every user; the arm only decides which score orders the list), so the latency and degradation columns compare like with like.
